title: FTX-26t Scenario-qualified multiphysics material optimization and browser studies
description: Plan 25.10 continuation of delivered ftx-ms1. Compose existing drape, source-thickness-dependent body/layer coverage, environment-qualified thermal transport and manufacturing evaluators into a bounded study on the same pattern/body/pose/environment. Every alternative must recompute relevant geometry/heat/process consequences, retain exact input identities and independently report unavailable consumers; no cached old pose/coverage after material edits. Keep scalar screening distinct from garment-level objectives. Expose declared fit/strain, signed heat, complete mass, material-aware sewing/cutting and dated whole-order cost objectives with admissibility domains, source uncertainty and explicit Pareto tradeoffs. Do not invent missing data or silently rank incomparable environments/protocols. Add browser study controls using existing wasm APIs, exact source inspection, cancellation and stale-output invalidation. Acceptance: real production-consumer equality, source/material/pose change regressions, reproducible frozen requests, bounded work, partial-failure display; empirical jacket accuracy stays behind ftx-tm2/tm8 and relevant thermal/process gates. Plan 25.24 adds explicit reported_bounds comparison for assembly_mass_kg through the existing native/WASM/browser study seam. Complete reported endpoints propagate only through fixed authored area and additive inventory; inclusive constraints require the entire range and strict Pareto dominance requires separated ranges. Missing bounds exclude while nominal mass remains visible; overlapping or touching ranges remain unresolved. Existing nominal policies retain their behavior. Unsupported drape/thermal result intervals refuse rather than imply generalized uncertainty or confidence. Remaining physical and other multiphysics uncertainty acceptance stays open.

title: FTX-26u Resolve M1 raw woven test units before calibrated sheet-law promotion
description: Plan 25.10 / ftx-tm2 targeted characterization. New built-in zagreb/polym17152013/M1 preserves primary Table 1 construction, conditioned areal weight/thread density and pressure-qualified thickness, plus original Table 2 KES extension observations. Source: Mahnic Naglic, Petrak and Tomljenovic (2025), DOI 10.3390/polym17152013, CC BY 4.0; see docs/measured-woven-m1.md. Obtain raw source/author clarification for KES load-versus-width normalization, bending dimensional convention versus printed CAD conversions, and Table 3 adapted Fabric Kit force units. Retain matched coupon geometry, direction, conditioning, replicates and uncertainty. Reproduce source observations before using existing calibration APIs; fitted laws remain estimates requiring consent. Never map finite-load elongation to breaking strain, copy CAD tuning numbers into tensors by name, split three measurement methods into three independent fabrics, or infer free loft from 1 kPa thickness. Validate on held-out coupons and retain explicit gaps for pair friction/width/thermal/pricing. This is one named specimen upgrade, not closure of the larger linen/leather/knit or garment gate.
